key_insight: Adaptive Bayesian weight selection helps quantum multi-objective optimization reach comparable Pareto coverage with fewer costly solver calls.
engineering_relevance: Reducing scalarized solves could make limited quantum-computing budgets more useful for exploring competing materials-design objectives.
method: BW-QAMOO learns a Gaussian-process surrogate mapping objective weights to objective outcomes.
Expected hypervolume improvement selects the next weight vector adaptively.
QAOA solves the resulting scalarized Ising problems to expand Pareto coverage.
evidence_signal: Across frustrated alloy benchmarks with 3–4 objectives and 10–12 sites, simulated QAOA required a median 33% fewer solves than random sampling at 90%/95% hypervolume targets and 60–74% fewer than a uniform grid; a paired Wilcoxon test supported the savings.
watch_item: This demonstrates query efficiency, not quantum advantage; validation on real alloy data and quantum hardware remains open.
paper_title: Query-Efficient Quantum Multi-Objective Optimization for Materials Configuration Search via Bayesian Weight Selection
